ABSTRACT A high-altitude electromagnetic pulse (HEMP) or other geomagnetic disturbance (GMD) can disrupt the reliable operation of electric power grids by inducing low-frequency common-mode (CM) currents. Flowing through grounded transformers, these currents can saturate the magnetic core and significantly degrade performance.
